description:
You are the frontend platform engineer at GlobalRetail Inc., a mid-size e-commerce company. The InfoSec team has mandated that all npm package consumption must go through an internal Artifactory registry rather than directly to npmjs.org, to enforce license scanning and prevent supply-chain attacks. You must build out the complete npm registry infrastructure:

- A local npm repository named 'npm-internal' (description: 'Internal npm packages - GlobalRetail') to store packages developed in-house by GlobalRetail's engineering teams
- A remote npm repository named 'npmjs-mirror' that proxies the public npm registry at https://registry.npmjs.org, providing a cached, audited gateway to public packages
- A virtual npm repository named 'npm-all' that surfaces both sources to developers as a single endpoint, with 'npm-internal' listed before 'npmjs-mirror' so in-house packages shadow any public packages with the same name
- A user account named 'frontend-lead' (email: frontend-lead@globalretail.com, non-admin) to represent the frontend team lead who will manage the internal packages
- A group named 'frontend-developers' for all GlobalRetail frontend engineers
- The user 'frontend-lead' must be a member of 'frontend-developers'
- A permission target named 'frontend-npm-perms' that grants the 'frontend-developers' group Deploy and Read access on 'npm-internal'

All seven requirements must be fulfilled. Artifactory is at http://localhost:8082 (admin / password).
